stem: If $A$ and $B$ are symmetric matrices of same order such that $AB + BA = X$ and $AB - BA = Y$, then $(XY)^T =$
solution:
$(XY)^T = Y^TX^T$. Since $A, B$ are symmetric, $X^T = (AB + BA)^T = B^TA^T + A^TB^T = BA + AB = X$ and $Y^T = (AB - BA)^T = BA - AB = -Y$.

$\therefore (XY)^T = Y^TX^T = (-Y)X = -YX$

(Equivalently, expanding: $(XY)^T = (BA)(BA) + (BA)(AB) - (AB)(BA) - (AB)(AB) = (BA - AB)(BA + AB) = -YX$.)

stem: If the variance of the data $2, 3, 5, 8, 12$ is $\sigma^2$ and the mean deviation from the median for this data is M, then $\sigma^2 - \text{M} =$
solution:
Mean $= \dfrac{2 + 3 + 5 + 8 + 12}{5} = 6$, $\sigma^2 = \dfrac{16 + 9 + 1 + 4 + 36}{5} = 13.2$

Median $m = 5$. Mean deviation about median $= \dfrac{\sum|x_i - m|}{n} = \dfrac{3 + 2 + 0 + 3 + 7}{5} = 3$

$\sigma^2 - M = 13.2 - 3 = 10.2$

stem: Given a real valued function $f$ such that $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{\tan^2\{x\}}{x^2 - [x]^2} & \text{for } x > 0 \\ 1 & \text{for } x = 0 \\ \sqrt{\{x\}\cot\{x\}} & \text{for } x < 0 \end{cases}$ Then
solution:
$\lim\limits_{x\to0^-} f(x) = \lim\limits_{h\to0}\sqrt{\{-h\}\cot\{-h\}} = \lim\limits_{h\to0}\sqrt{(1 - h)\cot(1 - h)} = \sqrt{\cot 1}$

$\lim\limits_{x\to0^+} f(x) = \lim\limits_{h\to0}\dfrac{\tan^2\{h\}}{h^2 - [h]^2} = \lim\limits_{h\to0}\dfrac{\tan^2 h}{h^2} = 1$

$\therefore \lim\limits_{x\to0} f(x)$ does not exist.

stem: If $p$ and $q$ be the longest and the shortest distance respectively of the point $(-7, 2)$ from any point $(\alpha, \beta)$ on the curve whose equation is $x^2 + y^2 - 10x - 14y - 51 = 0$, then the G.M. of $p$ is
solution:
Centre $C = (5, 7)$, radius $= \sqrt{5^2 + 7^2 + 51} = 5\sqrt{5}$

$PC = \sqrt{12^2 + 5^2} = 13 \Rightarrow q = PA = 13 - 5\sqrt{5}$ and $p = PB = 13 + 5\sqrt{5}$

G.M. of $p$ and $q$ $= \sqrt{pq} = \sqrt{(13 - 5\sqrt{5})(13 + 5\sqrt{5})} = \sqrt{169 - 125} = 2\sqrt{11}$

notes: stem as printed says 'G.M. of p' (intended: of p and q)

stem: If the straight lines $2x + 3y - 1 = 0$, $x + 2y - 1 = 0$, and $ax + by - 1 = 0$ form a triangle with the origin as the orthocentre, then $(a, b)$ is equal to
solution:
Point A is the intersection of AB ($2x + 3y = 1$) and AC ($x + 2y = 1$). A line through A: $(x + 2y - 1) + \lambda(2x + 3y - 1) = 0$ ...(i)

It passes through the orthocentre $(0, 0)$: $-1 - \lambda = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = -1$, giving $x + y = 0$ as AD.

Since $AD \perp BC$: $-1 \times \left(-\dfrac{a}{b}\right) = -1 \Rightarrow a + b = 0$

Similarly, BE $\perp$ CA gives $a + 2b = 8$.

Solving: $a = -8$, $b = 8$

If $z, \bar{z}, -z, -\bar{z}$ form a rectangle of area $2\sqrt{3}$ square units, then one such $z$ is
solution:
Let $z = x + iy$, so $\bar{z} = x - iy$. The vertices of the rectangle are $(x, y), (x, -y), (-x, -y), (-x, y)$.

Area $= (2x)(2y) = 4xy = 2\sqrt{3} \Rightarrow 2xy = \sqrt{3}$

$x = \dfrac{1}{2}$, $y = \sqrt{3}$ satisfies this, so $z = \dfrac{1}{2} + \sqrt{3}i$
